name: Ottawa Knee Rule

citations.text: Stiell IG, Greenberg GH, Wells GA, et al. Prospective validation of a decision rule for the use of radiography in acute knee injuries. JAMA. 1996;275(8):611-615.

validated_population: Adults 18 and older with an acute knee injury in the emergency department.
self_report_note: The rule was validated with a clinician examining the knee. Self-examination is less reliable. The rule does not apply to injuries more than 7 days old.
license_note: Published clinical decision rule; criteria are not a copyrighted instrument. Question wording is original to OLA BOT.

red_flags.question: Is the knee bent at an odd angle, is the kneecap visibly out of place, or is bone showing through the skin?
red_flags.help: Answer yes for an obvious deformity or an open wound over the knee.

red_flags.question: Is the lower leg or foot cold, pale, blue, or numb?
red_flags.help: Compare with the other leg. These signs can mean poor blood flow or nerve injury.

items.question: Are you 55 years or older?
items.help: Older adults have a higher chance of a fracture after a knee injury.

items.question: When you press around the knee, is the kneecap the ONLY bony spot that hurts?
items.help: Press on the kneecap and on the bones around it. Answer yes if only the kneecap is tender.

items.question: Press on the bony bump on the OUTER side of the leg, just below the knee. Is it painful to press?
items.help: This bump (head of the fibula) is on the outside of the leg, about 1 inch below the knee joint.

items.question: Are you unable to bend the knee to a right angle (90°, like sitting in a chair)?
items.help: Sit and try to bend the knee so your lower leg is straight down. Answer yes if you cannot bend that far.

items.question: Were you unable to take 4 steps right after the injury, AND are you still unable now? (Limping counts as able.)
items.help: Answer yes only if you could not take 4 steps on your own, even limping, both right after the injury and now.
items.trace_label: Unable to bear weight (4 steps) immediately and now

scoring.threshold_text: Knee X-ray if any one of: age 55+, isolated kneecap tenderness, fibula head tenderness, unable to bend to 90°, or unable to walk 4 steps. Otherwise no X-ray.

xray.label: X-ray recommended
xray.interpretation: Your answers meet at least one Ottawa criterion. A fracture is possible and needs to be ruled out.

care.where_detail: Urgent care clinic with on-site X-ray. Call ahead to confirm X-ray is available.
ed_redirect: Kneecap or bone out of place
self_care: Keep weight off the leg until examined.
Ice for 15 minutes at a time and elevate the leg.

no_xray.label: X-ray not needed
no_xray.interpretation: No Ottawa criteria are present. A fracture is unlikely. Ligament or cartilage injuries are still possible and do not show on X-ray.
no_xray.recommendation: Treat at home. Get an exam if the knee gives way, locks, or is not improving.

care.within: Manage at home; see primary care or orthopedics within 1 week if not improving
care.where_detail: Home care. Book a primary care or orthopedics visit within 1 week if the knee gives way, locks, or stays swollen.
ed_redirect: Leg becomes cold, pale, or numb
self_care: Rest, ice 15 minutes at a time, compression wrap, and elevate the leg.
Acetaminophen or ibuprofen as labeled for pain.
